expectedBehavior: The revised design remains design-only until its new design review pipeline and Dexter acceptance close; no reader can mistake the current scheduling truth for implementation permission.
All 150 standards entries referenced by the manifest use actual matrix IDs and remain traceable to their review or mechanical enforcement destination.

The one 105th audit read returns a human-readable, authorized, sanitized history for every one of the 12 approved entity types without creating a cross-owner fact owner or a second authorization model.

findings.title: 唯一 current Roadmap 仍把已停止的 R5 实施声明为进行中
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md requires only the current Roadmap's explicit authorization to start a step. The hash-verified Roadmap CURRENT_* says R5_WHOLE_SCOPE_IMPLEMENTATION_IN_PROGRESS, R5_WHOLE_SCOPE_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED, and directs U01 implementation; its line 120 also says R5_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED=true. The later exact authorization, hash 358c..., explicitly says R5_REVISED_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED=false and stops the ongoing R5 implementation while the revised design is reviewed. The reviewed plan additionally conflicts with its own accepted-audit statement: section 0 says the wireframe was accepted, while section 11 still tells Dexter to accept or revise it before design review.
findings.counterexample: A fresh agent correctly following the Roadmap's own sole-scheduling-truth rule can begin U01 implementation from CURRENT_NEXT_ACTION even though the exact revised authorization forbids every app, contract, migration, test, runtime, seed, and reset write.
findings.risk: This is an authorization-control failure, not merely stale prose: it can cause prohibited implementation writes and makes the review packet incapable of proving which bytes are eligible for a later implementation decision.
findings.minimalFix: Before a new design verdict can be accepted, make the current Roadmap CURRENT_* and its nearby R5 authority prose explicitly state REVISED_DESIGN_IN_REVIEW and implementation/runtime/seed/reset unauthorized; make plan section 11 match the already accepted audit interaction. Bind the corrected scheduling source by hash in the revised manifest/review packet.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Creating a second scheduler or a parallel R5 authority registry would duplicate the single-owner control plane and create another drift surface; a bounded correction to the existing Roadmap and stale plan paragraph is smaller.

findings.title: Manifest Part C points to 23 non-existent standards rule IDs
findings.evidence: The reviewed manifest declares C.1 through C.4 as C.TABLE.01-C.TABLE.23. The hash-verified standards matrix contains those same 23 table rules only as C.T01-C.T23; jq readback confirms every C rule ID uses C.Txx. standards-coverage --phase R5 passes because it validates the matrix phase, not this manifest's semantic rule-ID references.
findings.counterexample: A reviewer following manifest C.2's C.TABLE.07-C.TABLE.12 cannot locate any matrix rule, enforcement destination, or review checklist, so a contract/face boundary omission can be presented as covered even though no real standards anchor was cited.
findings.risk: The mandatory Part B/C/D hit map is materially unverifiable for all 23 Part C rules. This defeats the stated trace/enforcement denominator and hides which rules are semantic review obligations rather than gates.
findings.minimalFix: Replace every C.TABLE.01-C.TABLE.23 reference with its existing C.T01-C.T23 matrix ID, then recheck each C group against its actual reviewChecklistRef and design location. Extend the manifest checker only if a mechanical ID-existence cross-check remains a recurring, one-line rule.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Renaming all matrix IDs or adding compatibility aliases would rewrite a frozen 150-rule denominator and duplicate identifiers; correcting the new manifest references is strictly smaller.

findings.title: 统一操作历史缺少 actor 显示名的 owner-safe 读取设计
findings.evidence: The accepted audit Journey requires actorDisplayName and human-readable history, and the reviewed plan's proposed audit shape contains only actor_type and actor_id while requiring a shared getEntityAuditHistory task read. It does not assign who resolves platform versus workspace actors, which owner API may expose the display value, what an absent/disabled actor returns, or where that sanitization occurs. Current production source confirms the gap rather than solving it: platform_iam.platform_audit, organization.organization_audit, contract.contract_audit, and workspace_iam.workspace_audit have event/detail forms; writes use detail_json '{}' and commonly omit an actor identity. PlatformAssetService likewise shows current owner APIs are narrow commands, not a cross-owner actor display service. Under the owner rule, a platform-access facade may not become an owner of copied audit facts.
findings.counterexample: An operations user opens STORE history after a platform or workspace actor changed the fact. A union of owner-local rows can return actor type/id but cannot produce the required safe display name without either an unspecified cross-schema identity lookup, an unsafe frontend lookup, or a copied actor name with no defined snapshot/redaction semantics.
findings.risk: The only new user-facing Journey can either fail its central 'who changed what' task, leak identity information across platform/operations boundaries, or induce an unauthorized generic audit projection/facade during implementation.
findings.minimalFix: Specify a small read-only actor-display contract: each audit row records the permitted actor identity and a sanitized display snapshot or its owner-local audit task reader obtains it through an explicit identity read API; define deleted/disabled/system actor output, platform-versus-operations visibility, and the exact redaction set. Make getEntityAuditHistory compose only approved owner task-read DTOs after the host entity authorization succeeds, with focused tests for platform actor, operations actor, unavailable actor, and cross-face denial.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A new global audit schema, projection, outbox, or identity replication would violate the current no-projection/no-outbox direction and adds a new fact owner. The explicit DTO/snapshot-or-read-API decision is enough for this one task read.

findings.title: 修订 design package 无法通过其声明为 ACTIVE 的 granularity validator
findings.evidence: Fresh production invocation `scripts/check/implementation-design-granularity --manifest doc/review/platform/2026-07-26-v2s-r5-revised-design-granularity-manifest.json --review doc/review/platform/2026-07-26-v2s-r5-revised-design-adversarial-review-round-1.json` fails `AUTHORIZATION_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORITY_NOT_FALSE`. The checker reads the manifest authorization artifact and requires a literal `implementationAuthority: false`; the exact authorization uses only R5_REVISED_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED=false in a text block. The manifest declares this checker ACTIVE and its self-test true, so its own package binding is not runnable.
findings.counterexample: Even a review JSON with correct identity, checklist, verdict denominator, and severity links cannot be accepted by the mandated mechanical gate because validation fails before it reaches those review fields.
findings.risk: The design cannot establish its required review closure and can falsely appear ready if a reader relies on the authorization's prose rather than executing the declared production checker.
findings.minimalFix: Add the authoritative front-matter declaration `implementationAuthority: false` to the exact revised design authorization (while retaining the explicit R5_REVISED flags), then re-hash and bind it in the manifest before rerunning the validator.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Weakening the validator to parse one-off prose or creating a second authorization binding convention would reduce a one-line mechanical rule's reliability; normalizing the active authorization metadata is smaller.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: Reasonable in direction: the accepted user task needs a bounded, entity-detail operation history, and the design correctly rejects a generic audit product, per-entity duplicate endpoints, and a second permission system.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: One shared 105th read operation and one Modal are smaller than twelve endpoints or a report surface. The smaller viable remediation for the findings is to correct existing authority/trace bindings and define one explicit actor-display read contract, not to introduce an audit platform, projection, or new schema owner.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The planned phased reuse of owner-local facts, generated wire, existing foundation primitives, and explicit seed/test controls fits R5. It does not fit the current authorization and audit-read ambiguity: proceeding would convert small design decisions into expensive and potentially unauthorized rework.

conclusion.summary: NO_GO (M=1, S=3, N=0). The solution direction is proportionate, but the sole scheduling source still authorizes forbidden implementation, the declared package cannot pass its own validator, the manifest's 23 Part C anchors are invalid, and the user-visible audit read lacks an owner-safe actor-display design. All four must be resolved and independently re-reviewed in the permitted second round.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: This is DESIGN review only. It does not authorize implementation, runtime, DEV, database/Flyway, contract, app, test, seed/reset, or any other business-source write.
